findings.problem: status is a bare String instead of a domain enum. Any arbitrary string (e.g. "deleted", "", null-byte) is a valid value, making illegal states representable.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code must string-compare instead of exhaustive-match on a total enum, allowing silent bugs from typos or unexpected values in status.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a `LedgerStatus` enum (e.g. `Pending`, `Sent`, `Validated`) with a derive `Display` for any serialization needs.

findings.problem: is_validated is a bool lifecycle flag. Booleans cannot encode multi-way state (validated vs not-validated vs invalid) and cannot prevent logically impossible combinations with is_sent.
findings.failure_mode: A ledger can be simultaneously is_validated=false and is_sent=true, or is_validated=true and is_sent=false — states the domain likely forbids. Bool flags encode partial, non-total state.
findings.fix: Replace `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` with a single `LedgerState` typestate enum (e.g. `Draft`, `Sent`, `Validated`) that makes illegal combinations unrepresentable.

findings.problem: is_sent is a bool lifecycle flag, redundant with status and prone to inconsistency.
findings.failure_mode: is_sent can diverge from status (e.g. status="sent" but is_sent=false, or status="pending" but is_sent=true). Two fields encode one concept without enforcement.
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent: bool`. Derive sent-ness from the `LedgerState` typestate enum. If a separate sent timestamp is needed, keep `sent_at_epoch_ms` but derive presence from the enum variant.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no preconditions. It accepts any LedgerWorkflow regardless of current state and mutates to "sent" unconditionally. No typestate guards the transition.
findings.failure_mode: A validated ledger can be re-sent, a ledger with mismatched is_sent can be transitioned, and any future lifecycle steps have no guardrail. The function silently permits invalid state transitions.
findings.fix: Accept the prior state explicitly (e.g. `fn mark_sent(state: LedgerState) -> LedgerState`) and return an `Err` for invalid transitions, or use a typestate pattern where `mark_sent` is only callable from `Draft`.

findings.problem: All struct fields are `pub`, allowing external code to construct `LedgerWorkflow` with arbitrary combinations: e.g. status="sent", is_sent=false, is_validated=true, or id="".
findings.failure_mode: Callers outside this module can build fully invalid `LedgerWorkflow` instances without going through any constructor or transition function, bypassing all invariants.
findings.fix: Make all fields `pub(crate)` or private. Provide a fallible constructor `LedgerWorkflow::new(id: String) -> Result<Self, Error>` or, better, replace the struct with typestate newtypes so construction itself enforces validity.

findings.problem: id is a bare String with no domain constraints (length, format, uniqueness). Empty string or arbitrary-length strings are accepted.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream lookups or deduplication may fail or collide with empty/invalid IDs. No compile-time enforcement of ID invariants.
findings.fix: Introduce a `LedgerId` newtype with a fallible constructor that validates format/length, and use `LedgerId` instead of `String`.

findings.problem: `"sent".to_string()` performs an unbounded allocation without checking allocation failure. The String id field similarly allows unbounded allocation on construction.
findings.failure_mode: Under memory pressure, `.to_string()` can return an OOM error. Ignoring it (implicitly here) means allocation failure becomes a silent panic or corrupt state.
findings.fix: Prefer a non-allocating enum variant or ensure all string fields are constructed through fallible constructors that handle `Allocation` errors.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied throughput/latency of mark_sent or any LedgerWorkflow lifecycle operation
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, cachegrind, or perf data) for hot paths
no allocation audit (e.g. `dhat` or `valgrind --leak-check=full`) for LedgerWorkflow lifetime
no second-ring review (black-hat or architectural drift) artifact present
no command evidence (cargo fmt, cargo test, cargo clippy) was run or recorded
residual_risk: The domain model is fundamentally broken: primitive types encode state machine concepts, bools allow logically impossible combinations, and all fields are publicly mutable. This is a structural violation of the Power-of-Ten. No amount of benchmarking or sanitizers can compensate for a model that permits illegal states by construction. The code must be redesigned around typestate enums and private fields before any performance or safety claims are credible.
